title: systemd, cgroup v2 and resource control
part: Part 1 · The box, the way the gurus run it
brief: Services are units, units live in cgroups, and cgroups decide who starves first. Change vendor units with drop-ins, never in place.

exercises.prompt: Every lab here assumes cgroup v2. What does `stat -fc %T /sys/fs/cgroup` print on a correct host? Predict, then run it on this machine.
exercises.explain: cgroup2fs. Current systemd only mounts v2, current Kubernetes refuses to start kubelet on v1, and Amazon Linux 2 reached end of life on 30 June 2026. tmpfs means the old v1 or hybrid layout; fix that before any lab.

exercises.prompt: You need to change MemoryMax for a service that came from a package. Where does the change go?
options: A drop-in, /etc/systemd/system/<unit>.service.d/override.conf (systemctl edit), then daemon-reload and restart
A cron job that sets it after boot
exercises.explain: Vendor units are replaced on upgrade; drop-ins in /etc override them key by key and survive. systemctl cat shows the merged unit, which is what systemd actually runs.

exercises.prompt: metrics-collector is OOM-killed on every start because its limit is below its working set. Someone removed the limits instead. Put back a sane ceiling: at least 256M, with MemoryHigh below MemoryMax.
exercises.hint: Under [Service], set MemoryHigh to something like 400M and MemoryMax to 512M. infinity is not a fix; it lets one leaking process take the whole box.
exercises.explain: Resource limits are a feature; the bug was the number. MemoryHigh throttles and reclaims before MemoryMax kills. Lab 5's VM 1 test checks that the fix lives in a .d/ drop-in and that MemoryMax is still set.

checks.name: limits are not removed (no infinity, no empty value)
MemoryMax leaves room for the 180 MB working set (256M or more)

exercises.prompt: Make this llama.cpp server unit safe on a shared host: localhost only, not root, restart on failure, start after the network is online, a memory ceiling, and basic sandboxing.
exercises.hint: --host 127.0.0.1; DynamicUser=yes (SupplementaryGroups=video render for GPU device nodes); Restart=on-failure; Wants= and After=network-online.target; MemoryHigh below MemoryMax; NoNewPrivileges=yes, ProtectSystem=strict, PrivateTmp=yes. On a real host run systemd-analyze security model-api.service.
exercises.explain: A model server is a network service that runs whatever the model decides to call. Localhost only, no root, restart on failure, a ceiling that throttles before it kills, and a filesystem it cannot write. systemd-analyze security scores what is left exposed.

checks.name: runs as a dynamic or dedicated user
waits for the network to be online (Wants=)
waits for the network to be online (After=)
systemd-analyze verify (advisory: the binary is not on this machine)

exercises.prompt: Which command scores how exposed a unit is (sandboxing and privileges), lower being better?
exercises.explain: It lists every sandboxing option the unit does or does not use, with a weighted exposure score.

exercises.prompt: Show only this boot's logs for metrics-collector.
exercises.explain: -b limits to the current boot, -u to one unit. Add -f to follow, -p err to filter by priority.
